title: Sudan's SAF and RSF Both Respond to US-Brokered Peace Proposal — RSF Accepts Truce, Rejects Withdrawal
detail: July 12-14, 2026 — Sudan's Security and Defence Council under Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan reviewed and responded to the US-brokered peace proposal advanced by Senior Advisor Massad Boulos (building on the Quad roadmap), asserting it remains the sole authority on war-and-peace decisions. Two days later, the Rapid Support Forces submitted its own formal response: accepting an unconditional three-month humanitarian truce for UN-supervised aid delivery to Darfur, Kordofan, Ed Damazin, and the Nuba Mountains, but rejecting the plan's demand for a phased withdrawal from territory it currently holds in North Darfur and North Kordofan. The split responses left the proposal without a common basis for implementation.

title: ASEAN Holds First Post-Coup Ministerial with Myanmar Junta, Then Separately Engages Opposition and Ethnic Groups
detail: July 12-16, 2026 — ASEAN foreign ministers held their first in-person engagement with Myanmar's junta counterpart, Tin Maung Swe, in Bangkok since the 2021 coup, with Thailand as facilitator and the Philippines (2026 ASEAN chair) pressing for concrete progress on the Five-Point Consensus. The next day, ASEAN Special Envoy Theresa Lazaro met separately with the junta's negotiation committee and with ethnic minority rebel groups in Thailand. Days later, Myanmar's National Unity Government held a video call with Lazaro insisting the process include a broad range of stakeholders, while the ethnic-armed SCEF coalition (KNU, KNPP, KIO, CNF) stressed its meeting was not formal dialogue with the junta. Myanmar's parliament had separately rejected the Five-Point Consensus as interference, underscoring the fragility of the reopened channel.
